Page Stack is a little web app for building [text assemblages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assemblage_(composition)) from the pages of classic books. 

**Links**

- [Page Stack][site]
- [How to use it][about]

With it you select text from across different pages of the book. This text selected is then composited together to form a single final page. [The site][about] has a much more detailed explanation of how this works and how to use it. This can be used to create little [poems](https://page-stack.mattbierner.com/#v=1&b=1600&s=bQAAAAlFAAIADVoABAYPWgAGCydaAAgADVoAGA0nYQAKEhdhAAoaL04ADAALVgAOABdiABAED2IAEBMhPAASABY8ABQAFzUAFgAQXAAaAxtDABwVJg), [art](https://page-stack.mattbierner.com/#v=1&b=21279&), or [just have fun](https://page-stack.mattbierner.com/#v=1&b=1063&).

The composite pages can either be viewed as text or in an interactive 3D view which is especially fun for word art:

<video controls autoplay muted loop src="../content/2026-04-13-page-stack/spin.mp4" title="Title"></video>

[Give it a try][site] and let me know if you create anything fun!
